Home.title: Frontend ecosystem: learn, start, build
Home.heroDesc: ViraStack brings free frontend guides, ready-made project templates, AI rules, and form components under one roof. Learn with Academy, then start your project with Start.
Home.ecosystemDesc: From learning to production, everything shares the same modern stack and DX language.
Home.ecosystemAcademyDesc: A current roadmap for becoming a frontend developer with React. Free guides from the fundamentals through advanced topics such as artificial intelligence, architecture, and testing.
Home.ecosystemStartDesc: Production-ready Next.js and TanStack Start projects in one command. Feature-Sliced architecture, type safety, and AI rules included.
Home.ecosystemAiDesc: An AI-native architecture kit so Claude Code, Cursor, and other agents write consistent code. Installs framework-aware rules in Claude Code and Cursor native formats, plus an AGENTS.md map.
Home.ecosystemMaskDesc: Accessible input masks for forms. Presets cover phone, credit card, date, and currency out of the box.
Home.ecosystemPasswordDesc: An accessible password visibility toggle for React. Lets users show and hide passwords safely and consistently.
Home.ecosystemGuideDesc: An interactive guide from raw HTML to an AI-native experience: modern web standards, one layer at a time.
Home.communityDesc: If you like ViraStack or want to support it, leave a star on GitHub. Reporting a bug, suggesting an idea, or contributing code matters just as much.
Home.metaDesc: Free frontend guides, Next.js and TanStack Start templates, AI rules, and form components. Learn, start, build.
Home.academyDesc: Built from official docs, conference talks, and independent writers, in order and without needless detail.
Home.aboutLead: ViraStack is an open-source ecosystem that brings long-term quality and architectural order to frontend projects.
Home.aboutBody1: AI makes writing code faster, but without the right foundation, technical debt, performance losses, and accessibility gaps become inevitable.
Home.aboutBody2: With a predefined architecture and best practices, ViraStack puts your project on solid ground from day one and keeps rewrite and maintenance costs low.
Home.aboutBody3: You need to know the right foundation before you can build on it. ViraStack also offers a free, carefully sourced roadmap for anyone who wants to learn frontend in order, from the fundamentals to advanced topics.

Ai.demoDesc: Same chat, different rule packs. The agent rejects the shortcut and ships the ViraStack pattern instead.
Ai.demoDataPrompt: Fetch the user list and show it on the page.
Ai.demoDataRejectBody: Server data belongs in TanStack Query: cache, retries, and shared keys. A one-off effect is not the project pattern.
Ai.demoDataAcceptBody: useQuery with a typed query key and shared api helper. The list is cached and reusable across the app.
Ai.demoArchitecturePrompt: Import UserCard from auth into the billing feature.
Ai.demoArchitectureRejectBody: Features must not import each other. That boundary is mandatory for the agent.
Ai.demoArchitectureAcceptBody: Move shared UI under components/shared; billing consumes it from there only.
Ai.demoFormsPrompt: Add an email field and validate it on submit.
Ai.demoFormsRejectBody: Ad-hoc string checks drift fast. Forms use React Hook Form with a Zod schema.
Ai.demoFormsAcceptBody: zodResolver + typed schema. Validation, errors, and submit stay in one place.
Ai.rulesDesc: One command writes 14 rules to <bold>.claude/rules</bold> and <bold>.cursor/rules</bold>, plus a rule map in <bold>AGENTS.md</bold> for every other agent.
Ai.rulesArchDesc: Always loaded: working agreement, naming, feature boundaries and imports. Agents don’t invent folders.
Ai.rulesDataDesc: TanStack Query for server data, Zustand and nuqs for client state, and one ApiError for failures.
Ai.rulesUiDesc: shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS 4, forms with React Hook Form and Zod. The i18n rule comes only with next-intl or Paraglide.
Ai.rulesQualityDesc: React 19 patterns, strict TypeScript with Zod 4, and tests with Vitest, Testing Library and MSW.
Ai.rulesPerfDesc: LCP, INP and CLS budgets. Measure first, keep only what helps.
Ai.rulesFwDesc: Only the detected framework’s rules are written; no cross-framework hallucinations.
Ai.howDesc: Three steps: detect, write, share. Added automatically when you create a project with ViraStack Start.
Ai.how1Body: Reads package.json and the lockfile: Next.js or TanStack Start, i18n library, package manager.
Ai.how2Body: Claude Code gets .claude/rules/virastack, Cursor gets .cursor/rules/virastack. Each rule loads when the agent touches matching files.
Ai.how3Body: A managed block in AGENTS.md maps every rule, so Codex, Copilot and other agents follow the same architecture.
Ai.cliDesc: Add ViraStack AI rules to an existing project.
Ai.cliForce: Also overwrite rule files you changed.
Ai.cliFramework: Explicitly set the framework <italic>(nextjs or tanstack)</italic>.
Ai.cliTr: Run the CLI with Turkish prompts and messages.
Ai.heroNewProject: Starting a new project? Use <start>Start</start>; AI rules come with setup.
Ai.ctaDesc: <start>Start</start> scaffolds a production-ready Next.js or TanStack project in one command — Feature-Sliced architecture, type safety, and these AI rules included.
Ai.rulesAll: See all 14 rules in the <docs>rule catalog</docs>.
Ai.cliAgent: AI tools to install for: claude, cursor or none. Default: claude,cursor.
Ai.cliDryRun: Show the plan without writing anything.
Ai.cliRemove: Remove the rules, the AGENTS.md block and the CLAUDE.md line.
Ai.cliDocs: Every command and flag is in the <docs>docs</docs>.

Start.demoVideoLabel: ViraStack Start setup: answer the prompts and get a project with AI rules ready.
Start.featuresCliDesc: Pick your stack; add optional modules and tools from one interactive menu.
Start.featuresStackDesc: Two equal-priority starters on the modern stack: React 19, Tailwind 4, Base UI, Motion.
Start.featuresFsdDesc: Standardized feature structure: api, components, hooks, schemas, and stores together. Clear ownership, scalable boundaries.
Start.featuresTypesDesc: Type-safe data flow: Zod env validation, typed schemas for forms and API, noUncheckedIndexedAccess on.
Start.featuresStateDesc: TanStack Query for server cache, Zustand for client UI, nuqs for URL state. Each owns one job.
Start.featuresAiDesc: Setup installs ViraStack AI rules for Claude Code and Cursor, plus three design skills. Agents write code that matches your architecture.

Mask.featuresRhfDesc: Formatted display in the input; raw unmasked values in React Hook Form. No sync hacks.
Mask.featuresPresetsDesc: Ready masks for payments, TR identity (TCKN, VKN), contact, and more. Pick a schema key and go.
Mask.featuresCardsDesc: BIN detection switches Amex 4-6-5 layout and CVV length automatically; Luhn-ready.
Mask.featuresValidationDesc: Algorithmic checks wire into React Hook Form errors, or plug in your own validator.
Mask.featuresCustomDesc: Define your own formats with patterns and resolveMask; no fork of the engine required.
Mask.featuresLightDesc: Zero runtime dependencies beyond React and React Hook Form as peers.

Password.featuresA11yDesc: aria-label, aria-pressed, and aria-controls out of the box, screen-reader-safe by default.
Password.featuresHeadlessDesc: Only prop bags; markup and styles stay yours. Same API for native or design-system inputs.
Password.featuresDefaultsDesc: Minimal show/hide icons ship with the hook so you can use it with zero extra assets.
Password.featuresMergeDesc: on* handlers chain and classNames merge; a11y props are never accidentally overwritten.
Password.featuresSyncDesc: Toggle locks with the field when disabled or read-only. Consistent UX without extra glue.
Password.featuresUiDesc: Works with the UI library you already use. shadcn, Ant and Chakra examples are in the docs.

SupportPage.title: Support
SupportPage.description: How to support ViraStack: stars, questions, feedback, and code.
SupportPage.intro: Support isn’t only writing code or opening a <italic>pull request</italic>. For a small open-source organization, <bold>starring</bold>, <bold>asking questions</bold>, and <bold>giving honest feedback</bold> also move the project forward.
SupportPage.starBody: Stars are one of the <bold>most critical factors</bold> for discovery and growth. If you like ViraStack or the projects catch your interest, starring the <github>GitHub organization</github> is the fastest, most effective way to support what comes next.
SupportPage.askTitle: Ask a Question or Open an Issue
SupportPage.askBody: Wherever you’re stuck, unclear documentation, or any confusing detail is valuable. Don’t hesitate to open an <italic>issue</italic> on the relevant repo; even a small question helps us find the right path.
SupportPage.feedbackBody: Share a missing feature, a confusing structure, or anything you think could improve. Honest critique and suggestions shape the <italic>roadmap</italic>. The right feedback is often <bold>more valuable than a PR</bold>.
SupportPage.codeBody: <italic>Pull requests</italic> are absolutely valuable. Before larger changes, opening an <italic>issue</italic> on the relevant repo and exchanging ideas helps your effort land in the right place.
SupportPage.closeBody: Whatever the size of your contribution, <bold>let’s grow ViraStack together</bold>.
SupportPage.thanks: Thank you for your time and interest. See you on <github>GitHub</github>!

AboutPage.title: About
AboutPage.description: The story behind ViraStack: from Turkuaz to an open-source ecosystem for frontend developers.
AboutPage.intro: ViraStack is an open-source ecosystem that brings long-term quality and architectural order to frontend projects. It offers free guides, production-ready starters, AI rules, and form components. The goal is simple: instead of rebuilding the foundation every time, <italic>build your product</italic>. It is made for developers working with React and Next.js.
AboutPage.whatBody1: <start>Start</start> is a production-ready Next.js starter with a Feature-Sliced structure. <ai>AI</ai> gives AI agents the rules they need to write code that fits your project. <mask>Mask</mask> provides accessible input masks for forms.
AboutPage.whatBody2: With Academy, you can learn frontend step by step, from the basics to advanced topics. Sources are picked one by one. Password and Guide are part of the same ecosystem.
AboutPage.principlesBody: Foundations come first. Starting fast comes after starting right. I avoid needless dependencies and detail. Everything is MIT licensed and open on GitHub. Rules are written for both people and AI agents.
AboutPage.learnBody: I've always learned frontend by building in public. Years ago, when Bootstrap defined the era, I shipped <turkuaz>Turkuaz</turkuaz>; a CSS framework I wrote to understand CSS deeply. That instinct hasn't changed. I still build to stay current; only how I build has.
AboutPage.formBody: The real time sink is usually the project skeleton, the conventions, the hooks you rewrite every time, and the rules that keep an AI agent from writing code at random. ViraStack sits right there: Feature-Sliced structure, starters, hooks, and agent rules; a ready foundation you can pick up and run with.
AboutPage.nameBody1: Before ViraStack, the organization was briefly called Vassale; a nod to a craft of joining pieces, and to bringing projects together. It was hard to discover, awkward for SEO, and too close to the English word <italic>vassal</italic>. So I looked for something else: workable as a global brand, still carrying a small thread of Turkish culture.
AboutPage.nameBody2: That word was <bold>Vira!</bold>; a call fishermen on Turkey's Black Sea coast use when hauling nets or lines, roughly “heave!” or “haul!” I paired it with Stack, and you get ViraStack: <start>Start</start>, <ai>AI</ai>, <mask>Mask</mask>, and the rest.
AboutPage.nameBody3: The turquoise in our logo is deliberate too: it comes from Turkuaz CSS, and I still love that color.
AboutPage.refsBody: When I look at <shadcn>shadcn</shadcn>, I see the path I was chasing with Turkuaz; he carried it much further. <tanner>Tanner</tanner> is a master of this craft. <tanstack>TanStack</tanstack> is both a clear bar for sustainable open source and an inspiration for the name: Vira + Stack. I'm grateful to all three.
AboutPage.closeBody: Yesterday there was Turkuaz. Today there's ViraStack. In tomorrow's frontend world, I'll be building something again.

BrandPage.title: Brand
BrandPage.description: ViraStack logo, naming, typography, and product colors.
BrandPage.intro: Logo, naming, typography, and color rules for the ViraStack brand. The same language is used across product pages and in copy.
BrandPage.logoBody: Use the mark alone or with the wordmark. The wordmark is always written as ViraStack; never apply CSS uppercase.
BrandPage.dotsBody: Six dots, one per product, always in this order: Academy, Start, AI, Mask, Password, Guide. Hover or focus a dot to see its name; each one links to its product.
BrandPage.namingBody: Don’t use the product name alone, for example <wrong>Mask</wrong>. Always write the full lockup: <mask>Mask</mask>. Short names alone are fine only in dense navigation.
BrandPage.typeBody: Black for headings, semibold everywhere else. ViraStack uses the primary color (#161616 light / #e5e5e5 dark). The product name stays medium italic in its color.
BrandPage.colorsBody: Each product maps to a Tailwind color. Only the active brand shade is shown.

Academy.authorsAmongSourcesExact: Among the sources: <name>Kent C. Dodds</name>, <name>Addy Osmani</name>, <name>Dan Abramov</name>, <name>Dominik Dorfmeister</name>, and <name>Luca Mezzalira</name>
Academy.sourcesDescription: The guides include only three kinds of sources: official documentation, recognized engineers in the field, and independent institutions.
Academy.contributeDescription: We can make Academy better together.
Academy.contributeIntro: We can make Academy better together.
Academy.contributeWhyP1: Working with AI agents sped up the work, but it also reduced how much we write and read code. Foundations and architecture decisions fade from memory over time, and there is so much to read that even choosing which sources to trust takes time.
Academy.contributeWhyP2: Academy offers curated learning for everyone from junior to senior, drawn from official docs, recognized engineers, and independent institutions. It is free and has no ads.
Academy.contributeHowBody: To suggest a source, report an error, or request a new guide topic, <githubIssue>open an issue on GitHub</githubIssue> or <githubPr>send a pull request</githubPr> directly.
Academy.contributeHowStar: <bold>Star and share:</bold> <githubStar>Star the repo on GitHub</githubStar>. Showing it to others helps Academy reach more people.
Academy.contributeFaqSourcesA: We accept official documentation, writing and talks by recognized engineers, and work from independent institutions (<italic>universities, standards bodies, engineering publications from large technology companies</italic>). Personal blogs and content with unclear identity fall outside these criteria. <sources>Review the criteria</sources>.
Academy.contributeFaqPaidQ: Are paid courses or affiliate content accepted?
Academy.contributeFaqPaidA: No. We build the guides from sources everyone can access for free.
Academy.contributeFaqErrorQ: I found an error in a guide. What should I do?
Academy.contributeFaqErrorA: <githubIssue>Open an issue on GitHub</githubIssue>. Naming the guide and the incorrect part is enough.
Academy.contributeFaqTopicQ: Can I suggest a new guide topic?
Academy.contributeFaqTopicA: Yes. Share the topic and the level by <githubIssue>opening an issue on GitHub</githubIssue>, and we’ll review it.
Academy.contributeFaqUpdateA: Each guide shows a last-verified date at the bottom. When tools ship new versions, related guides are checked again.
Academy.sourcesCriteriaOfficialBody: Documentation published by the team that builds a tool or a standard. They have the last word on how the tool works, and it is updated as versions change.
Academy.sourcesCriteriaEngineerBody: A maintainer of the tool, a member of the core team, or an engineer who speaks regularly at major conferences. What they write rests on experience tested in production for years.
Academy.sourcesCriteriaInstitutionBody: A university, standards body, or engineering publication from a large technology company that is not tied to a commercial tool. It rests on measured data and experience at large scale.
Academy.sourcesTrustTooltip: Which criterion this source meets: official documentation, a recognized engineer, or an independent institution.
Academy.sourcesCitationsTooltip: How many times the guides link to this source.

Guide.promptPlaceholder: Describe a component, page, or feature…
Guide.learnContentDesc: Every interface starts with content. Style comes after. The guide begins with plain semantic text, then builds on top of it.
Guide.learnStackDesc: HTML and CSS alone aren’t the modern baseline. React, TypeScript, Next.js, and TanStack Start set the architecture.
Guide.learnStyleDesc: Readability starts with layout. Tailwind handles spacing and alignment in seconds; no hand-written stylesheet.
Guide.learnTypeDesc: Browser defaults feel unfinished. Pick a typeface in the guide and the tone of every step changes.
Guide.learnUiDesc: Compose with shadcn/ui instead of reinventing controls; see Mask format card/phone data and Password toggle visibility live.
Guide.learnAiDesc: Add light/dark theming, then finish with a prompt-driven UI: type a request and watch a dynamic interface appear.
Guide.step0Body: Every interface starts with content. Design’s job is to make that text readable. The web’s foundation is semantic content; we build style on top of it.
Guide.step1Body: The traditional web was HTML and CSS. Today’s standard is a modern frontend architecture built with <react>React</react>, <typescript>TypeScript</typescript>, <nextjs>Next.js</nextjs>, and <tanstack>TanStack Start</tanstack>.
Guide.step2Body: Readability starts with the right layout. Instead of writing CSS by hand, we handle alignment and spacing in seconds with <tailwind>Tailwind CSS</tailwind>.
Guide.step3Body: The browser’s default fonts make a product feel unfinished. Typography sets the tone of the interface; choosing a font changes the visual language of every step.
Guide.step4Body: Building accessible components from scratch wastes time. With <shadcn>shadcn/ui</shadcn> we compose flexible structures, and ready-made masks format card and date data with ease.
Guide.step5Body: Dark mode is now a standard expectation. Theme switches that respect system or user preference integrate in just a few lines.
Guide.step6Body: Development workflows are evolving. Instead of writing code line by line, we ship AI-assisted, dynamic interfaces with the right prompts.
Guide.step6Prompt: Make a map showing Istanbul; include zoom and location buttons.
Guide.step7Body: We completed the journey from plain text to an AI-assisted interface.
Guide.step7AcademyDesc: Free guides from the fundamentals to AI, architecture, and testing.

DocsAi.introductionDescription: ViraStack AI installs one set of architecture rules for Claude Code, Cursor and every AGENTS.md agent.
DocsAi.introductionHeaderDesc: What ViraStack AI does, why it exists and the one command that installs it.
DocsAi.introductionLead: ViraStack AI (@virastack/ai) writes architecture rules for AI coding agents into a Next.js or TanStack Start project. The rules describe where code lives, which libraries to use and how, so agents write code that matches the rest of the project.
DocsAi.introductionWhatNative: Writes 14 rules in each tool’s native format: .claude/rules/virastack/ for Claude Code and .cursor/rules/virastack/ for Cursor.
DocsAi.introductionWhatMap: Adds a managed block to AGENTS.md with the project’s commands and a map of every rule, so Codex, Copilot and other agents find them too.
DocsAi.introductionWhatFramework: Detects Next.js or TanStack Start from package.json and installs only that framework’s rules. The i18n rule is added only when next-intl or Paraglide is installed.
DocsAi.introductionWhatManifest: Records every installed file in .virastack/ai.json, so updates replace only rules you did not change.
DocsAi.introductionWhySame: <bold>One standard, every tool:</bold> a team using <claudecode>Claude Code</claudecode> and <cursor>Cursor</cursor> side by side gets the same rules in both.
DocsAi.introductionWhyStack: <bold>Written for the current stack:</bold> <nextjs>Next.js</nextjs> 16, <react>React</react> 19.2, <tanstackstart>TanStack Start</tanstackstart>, <tanstackquery>TanStack Query</tanstackquery> 5, <zustand>Zustand</zustand> 5, <zod>Zod</zod> 4 and <tailwind>Tailwind CSS</tailwind> 4. Every example follows its own rules.
DocsAi.introductionWhySafe: Never overwrites your files: rules live in their own virastack/ folders. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md only get a small managed block or import line.
DocsAi.introductionQuickP: Run it in the project root:
DocsAi.introductionQuickStart: Starting a new project? <start>ViraStack Start</start> scaffolds <nextjs>Next.js</nextjs> or <tanstackstart>TanStack Start</tanstackstart> with these rules already installed.
DocsAi.introductionNextInstall: <link>Installation</link>: requirements, choosing AI tools and updating.
DocsAi.introductionNextRules: <link>Rule catalog</link>: what each rule covers and when it loads.
DocsAi.introductionNextUpgrade: <link>Upgrade to v2</link>: moving a v1 project to the new layout.
DocsAi.installationDescription: Install ViraStack AI in an existing project, pick your AI tools and keep the rules up to date.
DocsAi.installationHeaderDesc: Requirements, the install command, choosing AI tools and updating.
DocsAi.installationReqFramework: A package.json with next (Next.js) or @tanstack/react-start (TanStack Start). Otherwise pass --framework.
DocsAi.installationReqRoot: Run the command in the project root, next to package.json.
DocsAi.installationInstallP: The CLI prints what it detected, then every file it writes. With no flags it installs rules for both <claudecode>Claude Code</claudecode> and <cursor>Cursor</cursor>:
DocsAi.installationInstallCommit: Commit the new files, including .virastack/ai.json. Teammates and future updates rely on it.
DocsAi.installationAgentsP: Use --agent to install rules only for the tools you use:
DocsAi.installationAgentsBoth: --agent claude,cursor: both. This is the default.
DocsAi.installationAgentsNone: --agent none: plain Markdown rules in .agents/rules/virastack/, read through the AGENTS.md map.
DocsAi.installationAgentsSaved: The choice is saved in .virastack/ai.json and reused by the next init. Run init with a different --agent to switch; the other tool’s rule files are removed.
DocsAi.installationStartP: ViraStack Start asks “Which AI coding tools do you use?” and runs ViraStack AI with your answer. In an existing Start project, add or refresh the rules with add ai:
DocsAi.installationUpdateP: Run init again. Rules you did not change are updated, rules a new version drops are removed, and rules you changed are kept unless you confirm. See customization for changed rules and --force.
DocsAi.supportedToolsDescription: The AI coding tools and frameworks ViraStack AI supports.
DocsAi.supportedToolsHeaderDesc: Which tools load the rules natively, which read them from AGENTS.md, and the two that need one setting.
DocsAi.supportedToolsP: Claude Code and Cursor load the rules from their own folders. Every other tool reads the managed AGENTS.md block, which lists each rule with its file path and when to read it.
DocsAi.supportedToolsOthers: Other tools that read AGENTS.md (Windsurf, Zed, …)
DocsAi.supportedToolsMapP: Native rules load automatically when the agent touches matching files. Tools without native rules read the “Always” rules at the start of a task and the matching rule before editing, as the map tells them.
DocsAi.supportedToolsGeminiP: Gemini CLI reads GEMINI.md by default. Add AGENTS.md in .gemini/settings.json:
DocsAi.supportedToolsAiderP: Aider reads extra files listed in .aider.conf.yml:
DocsAi.supportedToolsFrameworkNext: Next.js 16 with the App Router. i18n with next-intl.
DocsAi.supportedToolsFrameworkDetect: The framework is read from package.json. Use --framework nextjs or --framework tanstack to override it.
DocsAi.cliDescription: Commands, flags and output of the ViraStack AI CLI.
DocsAi.cliHeaderDesc: Every command and flag, how to read the output, and how it behaves in CI.
DocsAi.cliCommandInit: Install the rules, or update an existing install.
DocsAi.cliCommandRemove: Remove every managed file, the AGENTS.md block and the CLAUDE.md import. Files you changed are kept unless you confirm or pass --force.
DocsAi.cliOptionForce: Also overwrite (or, with remove, delete) managed files you changed. Content outside the AGENTS.md block is never touched.
DocsAi.cliOptionDryRun: Print the plan without writing anything.
DocsAi.cliOptionYes: Answer every question with its default, which never overwrites.
DocsAi.cliOutputP: This run updated a project after next-intl was installed. The CLI lists each file with a sign and ends with a summary:
DocsAi.cliOutputSkipped: ! skipped or kept, with the reason
DocsAi.cliExampleDryRun: See what would change, without writing:
DocsAi.cliExampleRemove: Remove ViraStack AI from the project:
DocsAi.cliCiP: In a non-interactive shell the CLI never asks. Changed files are skipped with a warning, and --yes behaves the same in a terminal. Pass --force only when you want your changes replaced; see customization.
DocsAi.installedFilesDescription: Every file the CLI writes, the AGENTS.md block, the CLAUDE.md line and the manifest.
DocsAi.installedFilesHeaderDesc: Where the rules go, what the AGENTS.md block contains and how the manifest tracks files.
DocsAi.installedFilesTreeP: Rule files are only written for the tools you select. AGENTS.md and .virastack/ai.json are always written.
DocsAi.installedFilesAgentsP: ViraStack AI owns only the part between the BEGIN:virastack-ai and END:virastack-ai markers:
DocsAi.installedFilesAgentsCommands: Commands use the package manager found from your lockfile (pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck, npm test, …).
DocsAi.installedFilesAgentsMap: <bold>Rules</bold> lists where each tool reads the rules and a table of every rule with when to use it.
DocsAi.installedFilesAgentsOutside: Your own text above or below the block, and the Next.js block (BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules), stay byte for byte.
DocsAi.installedFilesClaudeP: With --agent claude, CLAUDE.md gets an @AGENTS.md import line so Claude Code reads the block. The file is created if it does not exist; otherwise the line is added at the top and the rest stays. remove undoes exactly what was done.
DocsAi.installedFilesManifestP: .virastack/ai.json records what was installed. Commit it and do not edit it by hand.
DocsAi.installedFilesFieldCliVersion: The @virastack/ai version that wrote the file.
DocsAi.installedFilesFieldClaudeImport: created or inserted: how the @AGENTS.md line got into CLAUDE.md.
DocsAi.installedFilesFieldFiles: Each managed file with the sha256 hash of what was written. A different hash means you changed the file.
DocsAi.installedFilesManagedP: ViraStack AI creates, updates and removes only these:
DocsAi.installedFilesManagedRules: Rule files inside the virastack/ folders. Each starts with a “Managed by @virastack/ai” comment.
DocsAi.installedFilesManagedBlock: The virastack-ai block in AGENTS.md and the manifest.
DocsAi.installedFilesManagedNot: Anything else, including your own rule files next to the virastack/ folders, is never touched.
DocsAi.rulesDescription: All 14 ViraStack AI rules: what each covers and when it loads.
DocsAi.rulesHeaderDesc: Two rules always load. The others load when the agent works on matching files.
DocsAi.rulesLoadingPaths: The others carry file patterns: paths in Claude Code, globs in Cursor. The tool loads a rule when the agent reads or edits a matching file.
DocsAi.rulesLoadingOthers: Other agents follow the AGENTS.md map, which gives each rule’s “Use when” line.
DocsAi.rulesOnlyI18n: Only with next-intl or Paraglide installed
DocsAi.rulesCatalogCore: Working agreement: read before changing, minimal diffs, naming, named exports, error handling, comments.
DocsAi.rulesCatalogArchitecture: Stack table, folder tree, where code lives, feature boundaries and import rules (no ../ imports).
DocsAi.rulesCatalogReact: <react>React</react> 19 components and hooks: derive instead of mirror, effects only for external systems, React Compiler, ref as a prop.
DocsAi.rulesCatalogTypescript: Strict <typescript>TypeScript</typescript> and <zod>Zod</zod> 4: schemas first, discriminated unions, no any, as or non-null assertions.
DocsAi.rulesCatalogUi: shadcn/ui on Base UI or Radix, <tailwind>Tailwind CSS</tailwind> 4 tokens, loading, empty and error states, accessibility.
DocsAi.rulesCatalogForms: React Hook Form with zodResolver, schemas in schemas/, typed defaultValues, server errors with setError.
DocsAi.rulesCatalogApi: HTTP calls in features/*/api through src/lib/api.ts, <zod>Zod</zod>-parsed responses, ApiError, paginated lists.
DocsAi.rulesCatalogServerState: <tanstackquery>TanStack Query</tanstackquery> 5: key factories, one queryOptions per query, thin hooks, invalidation, optimistic updates.
DocsAi.rulesCatalogClientState: <zustand>Zustand</zustand> 5 stores with selectors and useShallow, URL state with nuqs, SSR-safe persistence.
DocsAi.rulesCatalogI18n: Messages in messages/, no hardcoded strings, typed keys; next-intl and Paraglide specifics.
DocsAi.rulesCatalogPerformance: LCP, INP and CLS budgets, measure before optimizing, images, fonts and scripts.
DocsAi.rulesCatalogTesting: <vitest>Vitest</vitest>, Testing Library and MSW: behavior over implementation, role queries, HTTP mocked with MSW.
DocsAi.rulesCatalogNextjs: App Router: Server Components, async params, Server Actions, "use cache", proxy.ts, next/image and next/font.
DocsAi.rulesCatalogTanstackStart: File routes, loaders with ensureQueryData, server functions with createServerFn, middleware, head().
DocsAi.rulesConditionalFramework: nextjs is installed only in Next.js projects, tanstack-start only in TanStack Start projects.
DocsAi.rulesConditionalI18n: i18n is installed only when next-intl or @inlang/paraglide-js is a dependency. Add the library later and run init again to get it.
DocsAi.rulesConditionalLines: Rules shared by both frameworks keep only the lines for yours, for example the QueryProvider setup in server-state.
DocsAi.rulesConditionalCommands: Commands inside the rules (lint, typecheck, test, shadcn add) use your package manager.
DocsAi.customizationDescription: Add your own rules, opt out of a rule by name, and know when to use --force.
DocsAi.customizationHeaderDesc: Keep project rules next to ViraStack’s, override a rule by name, and decide what happens to edited files.
DocsAi.customizationOwnP: Put project rules next to the virastack/ folder, not inside it. ViraStack AI never reads, changes or deletes them:
DocsAi.customizationOwnAgents: For other agents, write project instructions in AGENTS.md above or below the virastack-ai block.
DocsAi.customizationOverrideP: The block tells agents to follow every ViraStack rule unless a project instruction names the rule it overrides. Name it in your own rule file or in AGENTS.md:
DocsAi.customizationEditingAsk: init notices the change from the manifest hash and asks before overwriting it.
DocsAi.customizationEditingCi: In CI, or with --yes, the file is skipped and keeps your version, so it no longer gets updates.
DocsAi.customizationEditingPrefer: Prefer your own rule file over editing a managed one: you keep your change and still get updates.
DocsAi.customizationForceP: Use --force when you want to drop your edits to managed files and take the current version:
DocsAi.customizationForceSafe: With remove, --force also deletes managed files you changed. In both cases your own rule files and text outside the AGENTS.md block stay.
DocsAi.upgradeDescription: Move a project from ViraStack AI v1 to v2 with one command.
DocsAi.upgradeHeaderDesc: What changed, the one command that migrates, what to check by hand, and how to roll back.
DocsAi.upgradeChangedLocation: Rules moved from .cursor/rules/*.mdc to .cursor/rules/virastack/, and Claude Code gets its own copy in .claude/rules/virastack/. See installed files.
DocsAi.upgradeChangedDocs: docs/architecture-guide.md became the always-loaded architecture rule. docs/MEMORIES.md is gone.
DocsAi.upgradeChangedAgents: AGENTS.md is no longer replaced. ViraStack writes only its virastack-ai block.
DocsAi.upgradeChangedNext: The Next.js block (nextjs-agent-rules) is no longer written by ViraStack AI. Next.js and ViraStack Start add it to new projects; the copy v1 wrote is removed if you never edited it.
DocsAi.upgradeChangedConstants: features/*/data/ became constants/, and the rules no longer use the @/data alias or *.data.ts files.
DocsAi.upgradeCommandP: Commit or stash your work, then run in the project root:
DocsAi.upgradeCommandDeletes: v1 rule files and docs/ files you never edited are removed.
DocsAi.upgradeCommandKeeps: v1 files you edited are kept and listed, so you can move your changes and delete them yourself.
DocsAi.upgradeCommandAgents: An unedited v1 AGENTS.md is replaced by the new block. If you edited it, your content is kept, the block is added below it and the CLI warns you.
DocsAi.upgradeCommandDryRun: Lines marked (v1) are the migration. Add --dry-run to see them before anything is written.
DocsAi.upgradeChecklistKept: <bold>Kept v1 rule files:</bold> move your changes into your own rule file (see <customization>customization</customization>), then delete the old file.
DocsAi.upgradeChecklistAgents: Old AGENTS.md content: if the CLI warned you, remove the v1 part above the block so agents do not get duplicate instructions.
DocsAi.upgradeChecklistMemories: Filled-in docs/MEMORIES.md: it is kept. Move what is still useful into AGENTS.md outside the block, then delete it.
DocsAi.upgradeChecklistData: @/data in your code: rename data/ folders to constants/ and remove the alias from tsconfig.json, or agents will keep two patterns.
DocsAi.upgradeRollbackP: Remove v2, then install v1 again:
DocsAi.upgradeRollbackArchive: The v1 documentation stays in the <archive>v1 archive</archive>.
DocsAi.changelogHeaderDesc: What changed in each ViraStack AI release.
DocsAi.changelogBreakingLayout: Rules install to .claude/rules/virastack/ and .cursor/rules/virastack/, or .agents/rules/virastack/ with --agent none. docs/MEMORIES.md and docs/architecture-guide.md are no longer written.
DocsAi.changelogBreakingRenamed: Five rules were renamed and the architecture guide became the architecture rule. See the rename table.
DocsAi.changelogBreakingAgents: AGENTS.md is no longer replaced; only the virastack-ai block is written.
DocsAi.changelogAddedManifest: The .virastack/ai.json manifest: updates replace untouched rules, ask before overwriting edited ones and remove dropped ones.
DocsAi.changelogAddedMigration: Automatic v1 migration: unedited v1 files are removed, edited ones are kept and listed.
DocsAi.changelogAddedPackageManager: Commands in the rules use the detected package manager.
DocsAi.changelogAddedConditional: The i18n rule installs only with next-intl or Paraglide; framework-specific lines appear only for your framework.
DocsAi.changelogChangedRules: All 14 rules rewritten for <nextjs>Next.js</nextjs> 16, <react>React</react> 19.2, <tanstackstart>TanStack Start</tanstackstart>, <tanstackquery>TanStack Query</tanstackquery> 5, <zustand>Zustand</zustand> 5, <zod>Zod</zod> 4 and <tailwind>Tailwind CSS</tailwind> 4, about 30% shorter than v1.
DocsAi.changelogChangedQuery: TanStack Query: one queryOptions factory per query, thin hooks, optimistic updates only when needed.
DocsAi.changelogChangedZustand: Zustand: useShallow, per-request stores for SSR, useIsClient or skipHydration for persisted state.
DocsAi.changelogChangedTesting: Testing assumes <vitest>Vitest</vitest>, Testing Library and MSW, as shipped by ViraStack Start.
DocsAi.changelogChangedPerformance: Performance keeps only LCP, INP and CLS budgets; accessibility moved to ui.
DocsAi.changelogRemovedItems: Chat-era rules (INTENTIONAL_TODO, the blanket comment ban), the @/data alias and *.data.ts naming, TTI and API p95 budgets.
DocsAi.changelogV132: <bold>1.3.2</bold>: UI delivery checklist, focus and heading rules, Tailwind breakpoints for responsive checks.
DocsAi.changelogV131: <bold>1.3.1</bold>: contract-first API rules, branded types, optimistic update template, “keep or revert” performance rule.
DocsAi.changelogV130: 1.3.0: framework isolation, framework-specific AGENTS.md, --framework flag, CLI tests.
DocsAi.changelogV12: 1.2: framework detection, overwrite prompt and --force, --tr, fetch-first API client.
DocsAi.changelogV11: 1.1: CLAUDE.md, package-aware rules, URL state with nuqs, naming conventions, Tailwind CSS v4 classes.
DocsAi.changelogFull: The full history is in the <link>CHANGELOG on GitHub</link>.

DocsAiV1.introductionHeaderDesc: Install command, options, rules and files of ViraStack AI 1.3.2.
DocsAiV1.introductionLead: ViraStack AI 1.3.2 writes .mdc rules into .cursor/rules/, plus AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and an architecture guide in docs/. It detects Next.js or TanStack Start from package.json and writes only that framework’s rules.
DocsAiV1.introductionInstallP: @1 pins the last 1.x release. Without it, npm installs v2.
DocsAiV1.introductionOptionForce: Overwrite existing rule files without prompting.
DocsAiV1.introductionRulesP: Rules for the detected framework, written to .cursor/rules/. nextjs.mdc is for Next.js, tanstack-start.mdc for TanStack Start:
DocsAiV1.introductionFilesP: AGENTS.md is written for the detected framework; with Next.js it starts with the Next.js agent block. Existing files are overwritten only after you confirm or with --force.

DocsStart.introductionDescription: Create a production-ready Next.js or TanStack Start project with a single ViraStack Start command.
DocsStart.introductionDesc: <start></start> is a production-focused CLI that creates a modern React project in one command.
DocsStart.introductionP1: It cuts configuration fatigue with <nextjs>Next.js</nextjs> or <tanstack>TanStack Start</tanstack> templates, Feature-Sliced architecture, strict <typescript>TypeScript</typescript>, and AI agent rules.
DocsStart.introductionP2: Optional ecosystem tools such as <mask>Mask</mask> and <password>Password</password> can be selected during setup.
DocsStart.introductionGettingStartedP: Ready to create a project? Follow <installation>installation</installation>. For flags and non-interactive use see <cli>CLI</cli>; for framework and folder layout see <templates>templates</templates>.
DocsStart.introductionWhyCli: <bold>Interactive CLI</bold>: guided setup instead of a long flag checklist.
DocsStart.introductionWhyProd: <bold>Production-ready base</bold>: ESLint, Prettier, Husky, Knip, Commitlint, and CI come ready.
DocsStart.introductionWhyAgent: <bold>Agent-ready</bold>: setup writes <ai>AI</ai> rules for the AI coding tools you pick and installs three design skills, so assistants match the project architecture.
DocsStart.introductionWhatsInP: Every template ships a Feature-Sliced layout, theme support, Zod env validation, and the same shared packages for state, forms, and UI. The full list with icons is on the <templates>templates → shared stack</templates> page. Optional multi-language setup is covered under <i18n>i18n</i18n>.
DocsStart.introductionOutOfScope: Auth and database are intentionally out of scope; the architecture is left ready for you to add them when needed. Tests come ready with Vitest, Testing Library and MSW.
DocsStart.installationDescription: Run the ViraStack CLI, pick a template, and get the project running.
DocsStart.installationHeaderDesc: Prerequisites, the install command, what the CLI asks, and what to do next.
DocsStart.installationQuickP: <nodejs>Node.js</nodejs> 20.9+ is required. pnpm is recommended; npm, yarn, and bun are also supported.
DocsStart.installationQuickP2: This opens the interactive menu. For silent installs and every flag, see the <cli>CLI</cli> page.
DocsStart.installationQI18n: <bold>i18n</bold>: do you want the multi-language template?
DocsStart.installationSkillEmil: emil-design-eng (emilkowalski/skills): Emil Kowalski’s design engineering for animation, interaction and polish.
DocsStart.installationAfterP3: Enter the project directory and start the dev server:
DocsStart.installationAfterP4: The homepage renders the sample <landing>landing</landing> feature. Delete it when you build your product.
DocsStart.installationFixmeIntro: Templates mark the first steps with <fixme>FIXME:</fixme> comments. Search the repo for that marker, then update these in order:
DocsStart.installationFixmeStep1: <bold>Step 1: Site metadata</bold> (<file>src/config/site.config.ts</file>): replace the default description and social links with your product name, copy, and URLs. Name and base URL come from <env>.env</env>:
DocsStart.installationFixmeStep2: Step 2: Remote images (Next.js only) (next.config.ts): add your CDNs or media hosts under images.remotePatterns. This FIXME exists only in Next templates; TanStack Start has no equivalent.
DocsStart.installationFixmeStep3: Step 3: API auth header (src/lib/api.ts): when you pick an auth solution, attach the token in buildHeaders (the commented Authorization: Bearer example). Shared across all templates.
DocsStart.installationFixmeStep4: Step 4: Env and assets: update name/URL in .env; when adding variables, keep src/env.ts and .env.example in sync with your template’s prefix (NEXT_PUBLIC_* or VITE_*). Swap favicon and static files under public/.
DocsStart.cliDescription: All CLI options for interactive and non-interactive use.
DocsStart.cliHeaderDesc: Interactive wizard or silent install with flags, suited for CI and scripts.
DocsStart.cliUsageP: Run the CLI interactively, or pass flags for a silent install. Prefer a guided flow? Use the <builder>Builder</builder>.
DocsStart.cliBuilderNameDesc: Folder name for the new project.
DocsStart.cliBuilderTemplateDesc: Which framework would you like to start with?
DocsStart.cliBuilderToolsDesc: Select packages to include, if any.
DocsStart.cliBuilderResultDesc: Copy the command above, run it in your terminal, and your project will be created.
DocsStart.cliCmdInit: Create a new project (default; also runs with no command)
DocsStart.cliCmdAdd: Add a tool to an existing project (<list>mask</list>, <list>password</list>, <list>ai</list>)
DocsStart.cliFlagI18n: Enable or disable the i18n template
DocsStart.cliFlagSkip: Skip dependency install. AI rules and design skills are still added
DocsStart.cliTip: Use <tr>--tr</tr> for Turkish prompts, and <yes>--yes</yes> for a quick install with defaults.
DocsStart.cliAddP1: To add a ViraStack tool to an existing project, run the add command from the project root:
DocsStart.cliAddAi: <tool>ai</tool>: runs <pkg>@virastack/ai init</pkg> (with <pkg>--agent</pkg> when given). Files you changed are kept.
DocsStart.cliAddTip: During init, mask and password are optional; AI rules and design skills are added automatically. Use add for a tool you skipped or for an existing app. Outside Start projects, run ViraStack AI directly.
DocsStart.cliTelemetryP1: ViraStack collects anonymous usage data so we can keep statistics (for example template, i18n preference, selected tools and AI coding tools, package manager, and CLI version). No personal data, project name, or file paths are collected.
DocsStart.cliTelemetryP2: If you prefer not to share this data:
DocsStart.templatesDescription: Next.js and TanStack Start templates, plain or with i18n.
DocsStart.templatesHeaderDesc: Four production templates: Next.js and TanStack Start, each plain or with i18n.
DocsStart.templatesFrameworkP: The CLI offers two main frameworks; both have equal priority:
DocsStart.templatesNext: <bold><nextjs>Next.js</nextjs> App Router</bold>: Server Components, Turbopack, React Compiler. The i18n template with next-intl is kept separate.
DocsStart.templatesTanstack: <bold><tanstack>TanStack Start</tanstack></bold>: type-safe routing and SSR. Uses Paraglide JS for i18n.
DocsStart.templatesI18nP: Multi-language support isn’t stripped from code; it’s provided via <bold>separate templates</bold>. When the CLI asks “Do you want multi-language support?”, the matching template is copied:
DocsStart.templatesI18n: templates-i18n: includes locale routing and translation infrastructure, with messages in the root messages/ folder
DocsStart.templatesStackP: Aside from framework-specific routing, every template ships with these packages already installed:
DocsStart.templatesStackAi: AI encodes these choices as agent rules (see the rule catalog). Start also installs three design skills: emil-design-eng, better-ui and better-accessibility (details).
DocsStart.templatesStackExtra: Theme support and Zod-based env validation also ship with the template.
DocsStart.templatesFooter: Return to <installation>installation</installation> to set up, or see the <cli>CLI</cli> page for flags.
DocsStart.scriptsDescription: Which package.json script to run for day-to-day work, quality checks, and CI.
DocsStart.scriptsHeaderDesc: Use the right script for the job: local development, quality gates, and CI.
DocsStart.scriptsIntro: Every template ships with the same quality scripts. Framework-specific extras are noted below. Prefer pnpm; npm, yarn, and bun work the same way.
DocsStart.scriptsDev: Start the local dev server (Next.js uses Turbopack; TanStack Start uses Vite on port 3000).
DocsStart.scriptsBuild: Production build. Run before deploy or when you want to verify the build locally.
DocsStart.scriptsStart: Serve the production build (Next.js) or preview the Vite build (TanStack Start).
DocsStart.scriptsLint: Run ESLint with cache. Use while coding to catch issues early.
DocsStart.scriptsLintFix: Auto-fix ESLint issues, then run Prettier write.
DocsStart.scriptsLintCi: Strict lint for CI: zero warnings, plus Prettier check. Same gate as GitHub Actions.
DocsStart.scriptsFormat: Format the whole repo with Prettier.
DocsStart.scriptsTypecheck: TypeScript check with tsc --noEmit. Run before push if you changed types.
DocsStart.scriptsKnip: Find unused files, exports, and dependencies. Keep the scaffold lean.
DocsStart.scriptsQualityTip: Husky runs lint-staged on commit and related checks on push. You rarely need to run the full suite by hand unless CI fails locally.
DocsStart.scriptsFrameworkP: These scripts exist only on the matching template:
DocsStart.scriptsAnalyze: Bundle analyzer build. Use when you care about client bundle size.
DocsStart.scriptsGenerateRoutes: Regenerate the TanStack Router route tree after adding or renaming routes.
DocsStart.scriptsPreview: Preview the production Vite build (same idea as pnpm start).
DocsStart.scriptsCiP: GitHub Actions in the scaffold runs this sequence:
DocsStart.scriptsCiTip: If CI fails, reproduce the same order locally: pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint:ci && pnpm knip && pnpm test && pnpm build.
DocsStart.i18nDescription: Change the default locale and understand where messages live in the i18n templates.
DocsStart.i18nHeaderDesc: Only for the multi-language templates: how locales and the default language are wired.
DocsStart.i18nWhenP: This page only applies if you chose multi-language support at install time (the <bold>templates-i18n</bold> copy). Plain templates have no locale routing. Template overview: <templates>templates</templates>.
DocsStart.i18nNextP: Config lives in src/i18n/routing.ts. The scaffold ships with en and tr.
DocsStart.i18nNextLocales: locales / defaultLocale: which languages exist and which one is the fallback (en by default).
DocsStart.i18nNextMessages: Copy lives in <file>messages/en.json</file> and <file>messages/tr.json</file> at the project root (loaded via <file>src/i18n/request.ts</file>).
DocsStart.i18nNextPrefix: localePrefix: "as-needed": the default locale has no URL prefix (/); others use /tr/….
DocsStart.i18nNextDocs: For APIs and patterns beyond this scaffold, see the <link>next-intl docs</link>.
DocsStart.i18nTanstackP: Locales are defined in <file>project.inlang/settings.json</file>. Routing uses the <file>$lang</file> segment under <file>src/routes/</file>.
DocsStart.i18nTanstackSource: sourceLanguageTag: source / default language (en by default). languageTags: all locales.
DocsStart.i18nTanstackVite: App routes use /$lang: both locales are prefixed (/en/… and /tr/…). / redirects to /en (baseLocale). This is not Next-style as-needed.
DocsStart.i18nTanstackDocs: For Paraglide details, see the <link>Paraglide JS docs</link>.
DocsStart.i18nDefaultP: If you want to make another language the default:
DocsStart.i18nDefaultStep1: Next.js: set defaultLocale in src/i18n/routing.ts (for example "tr"). With as-needed, the new default loses its URL prefix.
DocsStart.i18nDefaultStep2: TanStack Start: set sourceLanguageTag in project.inlang/settings.json (and regenerate Paraglide so baseLocale updates). / will redirect to that locale; URLs stay prefixed for every language (/tr/…, /en/…).
DocsStart.i18nDefaultStep3: Update product copy in the matching message files. Keep <file>site.config</file> / SEO locale fields consistent if you expose them.
DocsStart.i18nDefaultTip: To add a new language, register it in the locale list, create its message file, and expose it in the language switcher. See the next-intl or Paraglide docs for details.
DocsStart.installationQAgents: AI coding tools: Claude Code, Cursor or both (both are preselected). Selecting none installs plain rules in .agents/rules/.
DocsStart.installationAfterOrder: The CLI then sets up the project in this order:
DocsStart.installationOrderInstall: Creates the git repository and installs dependencies, so husky can set up its hooks.
DocsStart.installationOrderNext: Next.js only: writes the Next.js block to AGENTS.md, which points agents to the docs in node_modules/next/dist/docs/.
DocsStart.installationOrderAi: Runs AI with your AI tool choice: rules in .claude/rules/virastack/ and .cursor/rules/virastack/, plus the rule map in AGENTS.md. See installed files.
DocsStart.installationOrderCommit: Makes the first commit, so git status is clean.
DocsStart.installationSkillsP: Every project gets three skills in .agents/skills/, whatever AI tools you pick. With Claude Code they are also copied to .claude/skills/. Skills are copied as files, not symlinks.
DocsStart.installationSkillBetterA11y: better-accessibility (jakubkrehel/skills): accessible components, focus handling and semantic markup.
DocsStart.installationSkillsOffline: Each skill installs on its own, so one failure does not stop the others. Skills are skipped only when you are offline; the CLI then prints the command to add them later. --skip-install does not skip them.
DocsStart.installationPrettierP: The template’s .prettierignore excludes AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .agents, .claude, .cursor, .virastack and skills-lock.json. ViraStack AI tracks its files by hash: if Prettier reformatted them, the next update would treat them as edited and stop updating them. It also keeps lint:ci from failing on files you did not write.
DocsStart.cliFlagAgent: AI coding tools: <list>claude</list>, <list>cursor</list> (comma separated) or <list>none</list>. With <list>--yes</list> and no value, both are selected
DocsStart.cliBuilderAgentsDesc: Which AI coding tools do you use? Leave both empty for plain rules.
DocsStart.scriptsTest: Run the test suite once with Vitest. CI runs it before the build.
DocsStart.scriptsTestWatch: Run Vitest in watch mode while you code.
DocsStart.templatesTestsP: Every template ships with Vitest, Testing Library and MSW ready to use.
DocsStart.templatesTestsSetup: vitest.config.ts and src/test/: jsdom setup, a renderWithProviders helper and an MSW server that fails on unhandled requests.
DocsStart.templatesTestsExamples: Example tests in the landing feature: a helper (get-initials.test.ts), an API function with MSW (get-users.api.test.ts) and a component (CartDemo.test.tsx).
DocsStart.templatesTestsScripts: pnpm test runs once and pnpm test:watch keeps watching. CI runs the tests before the build. See scripts.
DocsStart.templatesStructureBoundaries: ESLint blocks imports between features and parent-relative ../ imports, so the boundaries in this tree are enforced, not just suggested.
DocsStart.templatesTreeCommentTest: Vitest setup, render helper, MSW server

DocsPassword.introductionDescription: Accessible, headless password visibility toggle with a single useViraPassword() hook.
DocsPassword.useViraPasswordDescription: Hook API: options, inputProps / btnProps, visibility state, and programmatic control.
DocsPassword.accessibilityDescription: ARIA labels, type=button, aria-controls, and screen reader support out of the box.
DocsPassword.customizationDescription: Custom icons, text, input/button props, and style merging.
DocsPassword.helpersDescription: Core helpers, default icons, and mergeProps.
DocsPassword.uiLibrariesDescription: Password is not tied to a UI. Same pattern with shadcn, Ant Design, Chakra, or plain inputs.
DocsPassword.examplesDescription: Live previews. Click one for details and code.
DocsPassword.exampleBasicDescription: Simplest show/hide usage with default icons and ARIA.
DocsPassword.exampleBasicNote1: Default visibility is false; starts with input type=password.
DocsPassword.exampleBasicNote2: Eye icons come from the package; no extra setup needed.
DocsPassword.exampleCustomIconsDescription: Use your own SVG or components via icons.show / icons.hide.
DocsPassword.exampleCustomIconsNote0: show: when password is hidden (show button).
DocsPassword.exampleCustomIconsNote1: hide: when password is visible (hide button).
DocsPassword.exampleCustomIconsNote2: icons accepts ReactNode: icon, text, or any JSX.
DocsPassword.exampleCustomTextDescription: Use text like “Show” / “Hide” instead of icons. icons still accepts ReactNode.
DocsPassword.exampleCustomTextNote0: There is no separate text API; icons.show / icons.hide accept string or JSX.
DocsPassword.exampleCustomTextNote1: show: label when password is hidden.
DocsPassword.exampleCustomTextNote2: hide: label when password is visible.
DocsPassword.exampleDisabledDescription: When disabled or readOnly, the toggle is locked and visibility cannot change.
DocsPassword.exampleDisabledNote0: disabled: true → input and button disabled.
DocsPassword.exampleDisabledNote1: readOnly: true → input readOnly, button disabled.
DocsPassword.examplePropMergeDescription: Merge name, autoComplete, className, and handlers with inputProps and btnProps.
DocsPassword.examplePropMergeNote0: User props merge with base props.
DocsPassword.examplePropMergeNote1: on* handlers are chained; className is merged.
DocsPassword.examplePropMergeNote2: This example is not a form library; it shows prop merge behavior.
DocsPassword.exampleProgrammaticDescription: Control visibility from code with isVisible, toggle, and setVisible.
DocsPassword.exampleProgrammaticNote0: The hook return includes isVisible, toggle(), and setVisible(visible).
DocsPassword.exampleProgrammaticNote2: After blur or submit, call setVisible(false) to hide again.
DocsPassword.exampleProgrammaticNote3: When disabled / readOnly, the programmatic API is also a no-op.

DocsMask.introductionDescription: Type-safe, React Hook Form–compatible input formatting with ViraStack Mask: card, phone, IBAN, and more.
DocsMask.useViraMaskDescription: Hook API: schema, display vs raw values, and props spread onto inputs.
DocsMask.customMaskDescription: Mask syntax (9 / a / *), MaskOptions, and dynamic masks with resolveMask.
DocsMask.validationDescription: Built-in validators, custom functions, and error messages.
DocsMask.helpersDescription: Formatting and utility functions you can use outside the hook.
DocsMask.typesDescription: Exported TypeScript types and the MaskPreset union.
DocsMask.uiLibrariesDescription: Mask is UI-agnostic. The same pattern works with shadcn, Ant Design, Chakra, and plain inputs.
DocsMask.examplesDescription: Live previews of every preset. Click one for details and customization.
DocsMask.examplesPageHeaderDescription: Live previews of every preset. Click a title for details, code, and customization.
DocsMask.exampleDetailValidatorDescription: Produces a form error when an invalid value is entered.
DocsMask.exampleDetailFooter: See useViraMask() for the hook API and custom mask for custom masks.
DocsMask.exampleCreditCardDescription: Card number, expiry, and CVV together. CVV automatically expands to 4 digits for Amex.
DocsMask.exampleCreditCardNote0: Use card + expiry + cvv in the same schema.
DocsMask.exampleCreditCardNote1: American Express cards start with 34 or 37. In that case the card number switches to a 4-6-5 grouped mask and the CVV field automatically expands from 3 to 4 digits (resolveMask).
DocsMask.exampleCreditCardNote2: The card field has validator: 'luhn'; expiry has validator: 'expiry' built in.
DocsMask.exampleCardDescription: Credit / debit card number. Type is detected from Visa, Mastercard, Amex, and Troy BINs; the mask switches automatically for Amex.
DocsMask.exampleCardNote0: Numbers starting with 34/37 use the Amex mask (4-6-5).
DocsMask.exampleCardNote1: The form value is unmasked raw digits.
DocsMask.exampleCardNote2: Listen for visa / mastercard / amex / troy with onCardTypeChange.
DocsMask.exampleCardCustomization0Description: Show card type in the UI based on BIN.
DocsMask.exampleExpiryDescription: MM/YY format. The month must be valid and the date must not be in the past.
DocsMask.exampleExpiryNote0: Invalid months or past dates are not accepted.
DocsMask.exampleCvvDescription: 3-digit security code. Expands to 4 digits for Amex when a card field exists in the same schema.
DocsMask.exampleCvvNote0: resolveMask picks CVV_3 / CVV_4 based on the card field in the schema.
DocsMask.exampleCvvNote1: Defaults to 3 digits when there is no card field.
DocsMask.exampleCvvNote2: See the Credit card form example for integrated usage.
DocsMask.exampleCvvCustomization0Description: CVV length is tied to card type.
DocsMask.exampleCurrencyDescription: Currency format with thousand / decimal separators. The raw form value uses dot decimal (e.g. 1234.56).
DocsMask.exampleCurrencyNote0: Defaults (US/English): precision 2, decimal '.', thousand ',', empty symbol, prefix. Digits alone are the integer part (123456 → 123,456).
DocsMask.exampleCurrencyNote1: Uses the currency strategy instead of a pattern mask. Form raw always uses dot decimal (1234.56).
DocsMask.exampleCurrencyCustomization0Description: Override separators and add ₺ for TR locale.
DocsMask.exampleIbanDescription: TR-prefixed IBAN. TR is fixed in the display; the form value contains digits only. Includes mod-97 validation.
DocsMask.exampleIbanNote0: displayPrefix: 'TR' is not written to the raw value.
DocsMask.exampleTcknDescription: 11-digit Turkish Republic ID number with algorithmic validation.
DocsMask.exampleTaxNumberDescription: 10-digit tax ID number validated with the VKN algorithm.
DocsMask.examplePhoneNote0: Defaults to a common international grouping. No built-in format validator; only the mask is applied.
DocsMask.examplePhoneCustomization0Description: Override the mask for TR grouping with spaces.
DocsMask.exampleAlphaDescription: Letters and Turkish characters; consecutive spaces are collapsed.
DocsMask.exampleUsernameDescription: Slugify: lowercase, accent stripping, spaces → hyphens.
DocsMask.exampleDateNote0: dateFormat defaults to 'DMY'. Can be changed with MDY / YMD.
DocsMask.exampleDateCustomization1Description: Year/month/day order. Override the mask to 9999/99/99 so the year takes four slots first.
